newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW - Malaysia July trade deficit expected.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Malaysia July trade deficit expected.

text.p: Reaction to Malaysia's announcement on Monday of a 624.5 million ringgit trade deficit in July after a revised 551.4 million surplus in June was mixed.
While some economists said it was disappointing, others said this was expected.

"The figure is in line with our own expectations. It is actually better than some of the bearish comments that had been circulating in the market which had suggested that the deficit could be as high as one billion ringgit. This is a return to a more sustainable trend, following the previous two months' surpluses. Over the remainder of the year you could expect monthly deficits of roughly around this figure.

"What these figures suggest is that some of those lumpy (large, one-time equipment) import items are yet to impact on the trade figures, so the average monthly deficit should be around this figure over the rest of the year. There is still a possibility of a one billion ringgit plus deficit later in the year.

"This is mainly return to trend. If anything it shows that the export sector is still comparatively weak, but some of the negative effects of that are being masked by laggardly import demand and reduced payments for overseas shipments."
NIK AHMAD FAUZAN, Economist, Vickers Ballas, Kuala Lumpur
"The figures show an improving trend, but export growth was only about 2.5 percent for the month of July.
"Year-on-year imports did show negative growth, but the figures show that the import content in Malaysian exports is still high.
"On the whole the nubers are dissapointing. I was hoping for export growth of around five percent, but it actually came out roughly half of that."
